prefix: Reference images: the approved concept sheet of the giant robot 'Stilt-walker' (Design C), then a crop of its front view, a crop of its three-quarter side view, and an enlarged crop of its head. The Stilt-walker is an extremely tall, thin, graceful machine about 30 m high (a person reaches only to its ankle). It has: FOUR very long, thin stilt legs like a heron or a water strider, arranged as a front pair and a rear pair, each leg with a hip joint at the body, one knee joint about half way down and a small ankle with a small pointed three-toed foot; a compact body carried very high (about three quarters of the total height), a narrow dark carbon core covered by a pointed shield-shaped ceramic chest plate and two broad, drooping, wing-like ceramic shoulder shells; TWO long delicate manipulator arms that hang from the shoulders at the front of the body, each with one elbow and a large three-fingered hand with long slender clawed fingers that hangs at about knee height; a long slender neck rising from the front of the body; and a small, flat, elongated wedge-shaped head with a cluster of small BLUE sensor lights at its front tip and thin antenna whiskers at its back. Materials: smooth pale grey / off-white ceramic armour shells with fine panel seams over black carbon and dark graphite frame, joints, pistons and cable tendons. No red lights, no face, no eyes other than the small blue sensor cluster, no text or logos.

jobs.prompt: Make a clean ORTHOGRAPHIC model-sheet turnaround of exactly this robot for a 3D modeller. Five views in one row, all at the same scale, feet on one shared ground line, evenly spaced, not overlapping: FRONT, LEFT SIDE (head pointing left), REAR, a smaller TOP view (looking straight down, head pointing up), and a THREE-QUARTER front view. The front, side and rear views are true orthographic projections: no perspective, no foreshortening, camera exactly on the axis. Neutral standing pose in every view: all four legs nearly straight and planted, the front pair a little ahead of the body and the rear pair a little behind it, splayed slightly outward, knees very slightly bent; both arms hanging straight down relaxed and identical with the fingers gently open; the neck upright with a gentle forward curve; head level and looking straight ahead. Remove ALL moss, plants, hanging vines and dirt: the machine is clean and intact, as it left the factory. Keep every design detail of the concept: shape and split lines of the ceramic shells on the shoulders, chest, thighs and shins, the dark carbon joints at hip, knee, ankle, shoulder, elbow and wrist, thin pistons and cable tendons running along the legs, the three-fingered hands, the flat wedge head with its cluster of small blue lights. Plain flat neutral mid-grey background (#8a8a8a), soft even studio lighting, no cast shadows except a faint contact shadow, no scenery, no people, no motorbike, no labels, no text, no arrows, no border.
